# Claude Code Plugins

A collection of Claude Code plugins.

## Plugins

| Plugin | Description |
|--------|-------------|

## Install

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/JWPapi/claude-code-plugins
claude plugin install biome-lsp@jwpapi-plugins
```
files.biome-lsp/README.md:
# biome-claude-code-plugin

Biome LSP integration for Claude Code. Gives Claude instant lint diagnostics after every file edit — faster and more useful than ESLint or TypeScript LSP for catching mistakes mid-edit.

## Why Biome over ESLint or TypeScript LSP?

**Speed.** Biome is written in Rust and returns diagnostics in milliseconds. ESLint and `tsc` can take seconds to minutes on large codebases, which means Claude either waits or misses the feedback entirely. With Biome, Claude sees lint errors the moment it writes a file — no lag, no stale results.

**Less noise, more signal.** TypeScript LSP is great for type errors but floods diagnostics with hundreds of issues across every open file. Biome focuses on what matters during editing: unused imports, restricted imports, suspicious patterns, and code style violations. Claude gets actionable feedback without drowning in noise.

**Self-correcting edits.** Because diagnostics arrive instantly, Claude catches its own mistakes (unused variables, wrong import paths, banned patterns) on the very next turn — before they compound. With slower tools, Claude often finishes an entire task before discovering it introduced lint violations, then has to go back and fix them.

**Format-on-stop.** The plugin auto-formats all files when Claude finishes responding via a `Stop` hook. No per-edit overhead, no format noise in diagnostics — just clean code when Claude is done.

## What it does

- Connects Claude Code to [Biome](https://biomejs.dev)'s Language Server Protocol
- Claude sees lint errors and warnings immediately after each `Write`/`Edit`
- Auto-formats the project when Claude stops responding — no format noise in diagnostics
- Covers: TypeScript, JavaScript, JSX/TSX, JSON, CSS, GraphQL

## Prerequisites

Biome must be available via `npx` (installed as a project dependency or globally):

```bash
# Project-local (recommended)
npm install --save-dev @biomejs/biome

# Or global
npm install -g @biomejs/biome
```

## Install

```bash
# Add the marketplace (one-time)
claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/JWPapi/claude-code-plugins

# Install the plugin
claude plugin install biome-claude-code-plugin@jwpapi-plugins
```

Restart Claude Code after installing.

## How it works

1. **LSP server** — `npx biome lsp-proxy` runs in the background, providing real-time lint diagnostics to Claude after every file edit. The LSP only reports lint issues, not formatting — so diagnostics stay clean.

2. **Stop hook** — When Claude finishes responding, `biome check --fix --unsafe` runs once across the project, auto-fixing formatting and safe lint fixes. This replaces the per-edit formatting approach (which added ~2s per edit) with a single pass at the end.

## Notes

- Biome handles linting and formatting but **not type-checking**. For TypeScript type errors, pair this with the `typescript-lsp` plugin from the official marketplace.
- The LSP uses `npx biome lsp-proxy` so it works with project-local Biome installations.
- Biome reads your project's `biome.json` / `biome.jsonc` config automatically.
- The format-on-stop hook uses `biome check --fix --unsafe` to apply formatting and import-organization fixes.
